transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. My wife thought it would be a good idea for me to come in, just to... just to check in, you know? I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, really. 

It's just that... well, sometimes when I'm down at the domino table with the fellas, or even when I'm just sitting at home listening to the radio, I... I hear things. Not voices, exactly, but... messages. Like the announcer or the guys are saying little things that are meant just for me. Little warnings to be careful. My wife, she says it's just regular talk and I'm getting confused, but I can feel it, you know? It's silly, I'm sure, and I don't mean to make a fuss about it. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you ever see things that other people don't see?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that, Doctor. I wouldn't say I *see* things that aren't there. My eyes aren't what they used to be, but they don't play tricks on me like that. 

But, well... I suppose since we're talking about it, I should mention... sometimes, on those quiet afternoons when I'm just resting in the house, I do hear my old friend. It's usually just him calling my name from out on the porch, or maybe humming an old choir song we used to know. It sounds so clear, just like he's standing right there with me. It's actually quite comforting, really, just a nice memory coming back to me, I'm sure. I know he's not actually there. That's not too unusual for someone my age, is it? Just remembering things a bit strongly?
How often do you hear these messages or your old friend's voice?

Well, let's see... I suppose if I really think about it, it's been going on for a little while now. Maybe... maybe about nine months or so? But it's not all the time, Doctor, I promise. It's just on and off, you know? A little bit here and there. It's really not a bother most days. I hope that's alright... I mean, it's not too strange for it to happen every now and then over a few months, is it?
When you hear your old friend's voice, do you think it's actually him trying to communicate with you?

Oh, goodness, no, Doctor. No, no. I... I know he's not really there. I don't believe it's a ghost or him reaching out from the beyond or anything foolish like that. I promise you I don't think anything crazy. 

It's just... well, I figure it's just my old ears or my mind playing a little trick on me, bringing up a fond memory. Just an old man daydreaming a bit too loud, I suppose. I know the difference between what's real and what's just in my head. That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope you don't think I'm losing my marbles over it.
Do you ever find it hard to keep track of what you're saying or thinking, like your thoughts are getting jumbled up?

Well, sometimes... I suppose sometimes things do get a little bit, oh, what's the word... busy up there. But nothing terrible, Doctor, I assure you. Just... well, you know how it is when you get to be my age, sometimes you just have a lot on your mind. 

I'll be sitting there, and suddenly my mind is just running. It'll go from thinking about the old choir, and then right over to a baseball game, and then I'll remember a repair I need to do around the house, and then I'm thinking about my friend again. It all just goes round and round so fast, and... well, sometimes it's hard to hold onto just one thought long enough to explain it right if someone asks me what I'm thinking about. It gets a little jumbled, I guess. But that's just a normal part of getting older, right? Just having a lively mind? I try very hard to stay focused when I'm talking to folks, I really do. I hope I'm making sense to you now?
Do you often find yourself having trouble expressing your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

Well, no, Doctor, I don't believe I have that trouble. I mean... I know I just said my mind runs a bit fast sometimes, but when I actually open my mouth to speak, I try very hard to be clear. 

Folks seem to understand me just fine. My neighbors, the cashier down at the market... we always have nice little chats, and they never look at me like I'm speaking gibberish or anything like that. I don't think I confuse anybody. I'm making good sense to you right now, aren't I? I really hope so. I always try my best to be polite and clear when I'm spoken to, I wouldn't want to sound foolish.
Do you ever find yourself jumping from one topic to another when you're talking to someone?

Oh, heavens no. I... I always try my best to stick right to the point. I know it's not very polite to just go changing the subject when someone is trying to have a proper conversation with you. 

Now, I might tell a little story here and there, just, you know, how old folks do... but I always make sure to finish my thought. I don't just bounce around all over the place and confuse people. I haven't been doing anything like that with you today, have I, Doctor? I really do want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way. I'm doing alright, aren't I?
Do you often have difficulty finding the right words when you're trying to express yourself?

Well, I wouldn't say I have difficulty, exactly. I mean, sometimes a word might slip my mind for a moment, but... well, that happens to everyone my age, doesn't it? You just have to pause and let it come back to you. 

I'm usually quite good at explaining myself, I think. If I can't find the exact right word, I'll just use a different one, or explain what I mean another way. I don't just sit there stammering or anything like that. I try to make sure I'm always being clear. I haven't been struggling to find my words with you, have I? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you think your mind ever gets so busy or mixed up that it affects the way you speak or put your thoughts together?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say my mind gets mixed up. I mean, sure, sometimes I have a lot on my mind—who doesn't, especially when you get to be my age and you start worrying about little things? But it doesn't mess up how I talk. 

I always try to stay focused and make sure I'm putting my sentences together properly. I wouldn't want anyone thinking I'm losing my marbles or can't hold a decent conversation. I think I've been speaking pretty clearly today, haven't I? I really do try my best to give you good, sensible answers, Doctor. I hope I'm doing exactly what you need me to do.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disjointed or don't logically connect to each other?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I don't think my thoughts are disjointed at all. I mean, I like to think things through very carefully, step by step, you know? 

Sometimes, well, I suppose an older fellow like me might take a minute longer to get from point A to point B, but the connection is always there. It all makes perfectly good sense to me, and I try very hard to make sure it makes sense to whoever I'm talking to. I wouldn't want to sound foolish or... or confused. I've been making sense today, haven't I, Doctor? Everything I've said has connected up alright for you?
Do you believe the messages you hear are specifically about you or meant for you alone?

Well, I... I suppose I do think they're meant for me, yes. But I don't want you to think I'm making a big fuss over nothing. It's just... well, sometimes when I'm down at the domino table with the other men, or even when I'm just sitting at home listening to the radio announcer, they'll say little things. Just small messages, you know? 

My wife, she always tells me it's just regular talk and I shouldn't pay it any mind. And I know she means well, I really do. But... I can just tell they're warning me. Telling me to be careful. I'm not crazy for thinking that, am I, Doctor? I mean, a man has to look out for himself, doesn't he? I hope it's alright that I'm telling you this. I just want to be completely honest with you.
Do you think the messages you hear are real or just your imagination?

Well... I know how it sounds, Doctor. I really do. And I don't want you to think I'm just making things up or letting my imagination run wild. I'm a sensible man, I promise you. 

But... yes, I do believe they're real. I mean, when I'm sitting there at the domino table, I can just feel it. The way they look at me, the little things they say... it's not just regular talk, no matter what my wife says. And the radio announcer, too. It's like they're slipping these little warnings just for me, telling me to watch my step. 

I know my wife thinks it's all in my head, and I hate to upset her, but... I just know they're warning me. I wouldn't tell you this if I didn't think it was important. I'm doing the right thing by telling you, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you can help me.
Do you think anyone else can hear these messages or is it just you?

Oh, well... I... I don't think anyone else hears them quite the way I do, Doctor. I mean, my wife, she sits right there with me sometimes, and she just hears the regular words. She always tells me it's just talk, like I mentioned before. 

I don't want to sound like I think I'm... special or anything like that. I really don't. It's just that the men at the domino table, they have a way of saying things, and the radio announcer, too... the little messages, the warnings to be careful... they just seem to be directed right at me. 

I suppose it sounds a bit silly that an old man like me would be the only one picking up on it. I hope you don't think less of me for saying so. I just... I know what I hear, and I know they're warning me. But it's just me that catches it. That's a helpful answer, isn't it, Doctor? I'm trying my best to explain it right.
Do you often have thoughts that don't make sense to you or seem out of place?

Well, I... I don't think I have thoughts like that, no. My mind is usually pretty clear, Doctor. I mean, I might get a little mixed up sometimes, like anyone my age, but... my thoughts are just regular thoughts, I'd say. 

I try to keep a good head on my shoulders, you know? I wouldn't want you to think my mind is playing tricks on me or anything. Everything makes sense to me up here, even if it's just me that hears those little warnings. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. Am I doing alright with these questions?
Do you think there's any possibility that you're misinterpreting the messages you hear?

Well, I... I suppose anyone can make a mistake, Doctor. I really try to be reasonable about things, I do. I don't want you to think I'm stubborn or... or not willing to listen to reason. 

But... well, I came to see you because of this. It's just so clear to me. When I'm sitting there playing dominoes, the men... they'll say something, and it sounds like regular talk to anyone else, like my wife says. But I just know it's a little message for me. And the radio announcer, too. It's not that I want to believe it, but I know they're warning me to be careful. 

I've turned it over in my head a hundred times, trying to see it my wife's way, because I hate to cause a fuss. But the feeling is just so strong, Doctor. I'm sorry if that's not the right way to look at it. I'm really trying to be honest with you so you can figure out what's best for me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too difficult.
Have you ever stopped believing that the messages you hear are real, even if only for a short period?

Well, I... I try to, Doctor. I really do. When my wife tells me it's just regular talk, I sit there and I think, "Maybe she's right. Maybe I'm just an old man getting confused." I don't want to be a bother to her, or to you. 

But... well, I came to see you because I just can't shake it. Even when I tell myself it's nothing, the next time I'm at the domino table, or the radio announcer comes on... I just know it. I know those little messages are meant for me, warning me to be careful. It's just so real to me, Doctor, even though I wish it wasn't. I'm sorry if that means I'm not getting better. I hope I'm still being helpful by telling you the truth about it. Am I doing okay?
Do you often find yourself having trouble organizing your thoughts before expressing them?

Well, I... I try my best to be clear, Doctor. I really do. I know I'm getting up there in years, and sometimes folks my age can get a little mixed up, but I think I do alright. 

I mean, I might take a second to find the right word here and there, but I always know what I want to say. I don't want you to think my mind is slipping or that I can't keep my thoughts straight. I try to keep everything neat and tidy up here so I don't confuse anybody, especially you or my wife. I hope I've been making sense today. Have I been answering your questions okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think your thoughts are well-organized before you speak?

Well, yes, Doctor, I do. I really think so. I mean, I try very hard to make sure I've got everything lined up before I open my mouth. I don't want to ramble or waste your time. 

Sometimes my wife might say I take a minute to get to the point, but I just want to be sure I'm saying the right thing. I don't feel like my thoughts are jumbled up or anything like that. I like to think things through. I hope I'm coming across that way to you... do you think I'm doing a good job explaining things? I really don't want to be a difficult patient.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe in these messages at all?

Well, I... I know we talked about this just a little bit ago, and I don't want to sound like a broken record, Doctor. I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers. 

But to be completely honest with you... no, I haven't really had a time where I didn't believe them. Even when I try my hardest to agree with my wife, when she tells me it's just regular talk... I just know it's not. I came to see you because it's always there. When I'm sitting with the men at the domino table, or when that radio announcer comes on... they give those little messages meant just for me. They're warning me to be careful, and I can't just ignore a warning, you know? 

I know it sounds strange, and I'm so sorry if it makes me sound foolish or... or like I'm not trying hard enough to get better. I really am trying. But I just know they're talking to me. Does that make sense, Doctor? Am I still being a good patient by telling you this?
Do you still believe the messages you hear are real and meant for you?

Yes, sir, I do. I... I know we just talked about this a second ago, and I hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same thing again. I really want to do this right and give you the truth. 

But yes, I still believe them. Even when my wife promises me it's just regular talk, I... I just know in my heart they're warning me to be careful. Those men at the domino table and the fellow on the radio... they're sending those little messages just for me. That's why I came to see you, because it's so real to me. 

I hope you don't think I'm being stubborn or... or foolish for holding onto it. I don't want you to think I'm a bad patient who won't listen to reason. I'm just trying to tell you honestly what I'm experiencing. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm doing exactly what you need me to do.

target_item.manifestation: Doctor, I came because the men at the domino table and sometimes the radio announcer give little messages meant for me, and even when my wife says it is just talk, I know they are warning me to be careful.
target_item.reason: The doctor is probing the fixity of my beliefs about the messages and warnings, which corresponds to my delusions.

patient.answer:
Well, I... I suppose anyone can make a mistake, Doctor. I really try to be reasonable about things, I do. I don't want you to think I'm stubborn or... or not willing to listen to reason. 

But... well, I came to see you because of this. It's just so clear to me. When I'm sitting there playing dominoes, the men... they'll say something, and it sounds like regular talk to anyone else, like my wife says. But I just know it's a little message for me. And the radio announcer, too. It's not that I want to believe it, but I know they're warning me to be careful. 

I've turned it over in my head a hundred times, trying to see it my wife's way, because I hate to cause a fuss. But the feeling is just so strong, Doctor. I'm sorry if that's not the right way to look at it. I'm really trying to be honest with you so you can figure out what's best for me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too difficult.

inference.note: F25.0 was ruled out as the patient's symptoms do not align with persistent delusional disorder

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief in the messages is persistent over time
doctor.question: Have you ever stopped believing that the messages you hear are real, even if only for a short period?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Doctor, I came because the men at the domino table and sometimes the radio announcer give little messages meant for me, and even when my wife says it is just talk, I know they are warning me to be careful.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question asks if I have ever stopped believing the messages are real, assessing the fixed nature of my delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
Well, I... I try to, Doctor. I really do. When my wife tells me it's just regular talk, I sit there and I think, "Maybe she's right. Maybe I'm just an old man getting confused." I don't want to be a bother to her, or to you. 

But... well, I came to see you because I just can't shake it. Even when I tell myself it's nothing, the next time I'm at the domino table, or the radio announcer comes on... I just know it. I know those little messages are meant for me, warning me to be careful. It's just so real to me, Doctor, even though I wish it wasn't. I'm sorry if that means I'm not getting better. I hope I'm still being helpful by telling you the truth about it. Am I doing okay?

I mean, I might take a second to find the right word here and there, but I always know what I want to say. I don't want you to think my mind is slipping or that I can't keep my thoughts straight. I try to keep everything neat and tidy up here so I don't confuse anybody, especially you or my wife. I hope I've been making sense today. Have I been answering your questions okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

doctor.question: Do you think your thoughts are well-organized before you speak?

Well, yes, Doctor, I do. I really think so. I mean, I try very hard to make sure I've got everything lined up before I open my mouth. I don't want to ramble or waste your time. 

Sometimes my wife might say I take a minute to get to the point, but I just want to be sure I'm saying the right thing. I don't feel like my thoughts are jumbled up or anything like that. I like to think things through. I hope I'm coming across that way to you... do you think I'm doing a good job explaining things? I really don't want to be a difficult patient.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief in the messages is persistent over time
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe in these messages at all?

target_item.name: Delusions

patient.answer:
Well, I... I know we talked about this just a little bit ago, and I don't want to sound like a broken record, Doctor. I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers. 

But to be completely honest with you... no, I haven't really had a time where I didn't believe them. Even when I try my hardest to agree with my wife, when she tells me it's just regular talk... I just know it's not. I came to see you because it's always there. When I'm sitting with the men at the domino table, or when that radio announcer comes on... they give those little messages meant just for me. They're warning me to be careful, and I can't just ignore a warning, you know? 

I know it sounds strange, and I'm so sorry if it makes me sound foolish or... or like I'm not trying hard enough to get better. I really am trying. But I just know they're talking to me. Does that make sense, Doctor? Am I still being a good patient by telling you this?

doctor.question: Do you still believe the messages you hear are real and meant for you?

patient.answer:
Yes, sir, I do. I... I know we just talked about this a second ago, and I hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same thing again. I really want to do this right and give you the truth. 

But yes, I still believe them. Even when my wife promises me it's just regular talk, I... I just know in my heart they're warning me to be careful. Those men at the domino table and the fellow on the radio... they're sending those little messages just for me. That's why I came to see you, because it's so real to me. 

I hope you don't think I'm being stubborn or... or foolish for holding onto it. I don't want you to think I'm a bad patient who won't listen to reason. I'm just trying to tell you honestly what I'm experiencing. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm doing exactly what you need me to do.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient consistently reports hearing messages that are meant specifically for him, which he believes are real and not just his imagination, despite his wife's reassurances that it's just regular talk. This persistent belief in the reality of the messages, despite evidence to the contrary, is characteristic of a delusional disorder.
